text:
The Flyers' season has been swallowed by one name. Matvei Michkov has been the subject of reports that he wants out, the team says it has received no formal request and has no plan to move him, and Rick Tocchet told PhillyVoice the group handled the noise "really well" while admitting it's there. Meanwhile Michkov keeps playing like the best thing Philadelphia has: his line with Noah Cates and Porter Martone has taken 62% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and he was on the ice for 3.56 expected goals to 0.13 against Edmonton on Sunday.

The record is 6-11-6, 18 points from 23 games. The chances say this is a below-average team, 45.7% of the expected goals and 44% at five on five, but not this bad: the Flyers have scored 11.7 fewer goals than their chances deserve, and our playoff model has them about three points unluckier than their play. Sunday was the extreme version, 5.99 expected goals and a 5-2 loss with an 0-for-8 power play. The last ten games have been better by the chances (53%) than the 3-4-3 record shows.

Denver Barkey's first multi-goal game gave the week a lift. Martone, the rookie, is running cold, 4 points in 10 on 5.7 expected. Our simulations project 78 points and a 5% playoff chance. The thing to watch is whether the Michkov story ends in Philadelphia.
